subject.title: [Feature Request] Add config encryption for credentials at rest

question: Which credential-at-rest model should OpenClaw support for config, gateway/channel credentials, and provider auth profiles?
rationale: The code path is clear, but the permanent model changes key custody, unattended startup, migration, recovery, rotation, and auth/provider compatibility, so automation should not choose it without maintainer/security intent.

options.title: Design native encrypted-at-rest storage
options.body: Define a keychain or passphrase-backed storage model with doctor migration, recovery behavior, rotation guidance, and tests for config plus auth-profile SQLite storage.

options.title: Keep SecretRefs as the supported mitigation
options.body: Explicitly decide that transparent native encryption is out of scope for now and narrow this issue to docs, audit guidance, and SecretRef migration coverage.

options.title: Land partial hardening first
options.body: Use a smaller auth-store or resolver-backed step while keeping this issue open for config, backups, key management, and migration coverage.

recommendation.title: Design native encrypted-at-rest storage
recommendation.body: Define a keychain or passphrase-backed storage model with doctor migration, recovery behavior, rotation guidance, and tests for config plus auth-profile SQLite storage.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved decision spans the SQLite auth-profile persistence refactor, config compatibility policy, and current security docs where steipete has the strongest recent history signal.
